note:
Coverage. Thirty-seven pages, fifty-five measured regions on thirty-one of them, and every region accounted exactly once: fourteen figure rows, twelve table rows and twenty-nine exclusions. The paper prints thirteen numbered figures and eleven numbered tables, plus four appendix grids that carry the word 'Table:' and no number.

Region count is not exhibit count, and here it is the TABLES that go missing. Twenty-six rows sit against twenty-eight printed exhibits - thirteen figures, eleven numbered tables and four appendix grids - and the books do not balance by type: figures GAIN a row because Figure 5-2 prints in two boxes, while three printed tables get no row of their own: Table 3-2 on page 6 prints at y216.7-230.0 between two measured boxes and owns no region; the appendix's TEC grid prints at y608-718 directly under the box that holds two other grids; and the appendix unit-price grid is fused INTO that box, which spans y55.6-576.0 and carries both it and the twenty-one-row sector grid. One box, two complete data grids, and a third grid just below it with no box at all - the join between a region and an exhibit has to be made grid by grid, never box by box.

The appendix is not what it looks like. Pages 24-37 return zero images, no fill-image operator, and seventeen page-height regions that are 0.5 pt vector FRAMES - byte-identical at (90,72)-(506,759) on eight pages - drawn round live, extractable code. A census that trusted region height would call all of them plates; they are listings, and they are excluded as `not-an-exhibit`. The four real appendix exhibits are rule-only grids: horizontal rules, no verticals, no zebra, no units in header cells, captions above, none numbered.

Apparatus limits worth keeping. The page text layer is materially shorter than the page: page 14 returns 1,572 characters for roughly forty printed lines, and its prose, two inline display-maths strips and both tables exist in the render while only the tables survive as text. Page 16's coefficient matrix and page 18's equation band are absent from the text layer entirely. Nothing in this record was asserted from the layer alone where the layer was thin - families, legends, colourbars, merges and all grid metrics come from the crops, and the two grids with no measured region are named here rather than passed over.

What the custody buys. Every caption is a verbatim substring of the page that prints it except Table 2-1's, which is typed from the crop because it prints inside a JPEG; every lead and trail sentence is a verbatim substring within one page of its exhibit; every exclusion names page, bounding box and the reason it holds no exhibit. The citation picture is the paper's real finding: it numbers about a third of its exhibits and points at the rest, and two of its numbered references arrive after the artwork they name - one on the same page, one a page later - so 'first mention' here can legitimately precede or follow the print.

rules: Fifty-five measured regions on thirty-one of thirty-seven pages, every one accounted exactly once: fourteen figure rows, twelve table rows and twenty-nine exclusions [place.section_kind].

Caption side splits by exhibit type and only once against type: all thirteen figure rows print their caption BELOW the artwork except Figure 4-5, and all twelve table rows print theirs ABOVE the grid [caption.position].

Numbering is section-prefixed and restarts each section - Figure 4-1 to 4-11, Figure 5-1 and 5-2, Table 3-1 to 5-2 - with the dash spacing inconsistent between rows ('Figure 4-1 :' against 'Figure 4-6:') [caption.numbering].
The four appendix grids print a title that begins 'Table:' and carries NO number at all, so their numbering value is `none` while their verbatim is a real printed title [caption.numbering].

Table 2-1 is the only exhibit in the paper that OWNS its caption: the whole nomenclature grid is one JPEG and the title prints inside the measured box at ink y90.2-100.4, which is why its caption is typed from the crop and not from the text layer [caption.verbatim].

Tables scale with data and the grid grows only when a grouping appears: two- and three-row grids hold parameters and accuracies, five-row grids hold the four states, and the one twenty-one-row grid is the only one that needs a grouping column [table.rows].

Ten of the twelve grids are horizontal-rule-only; the nomenclature grid adds exactly one full-height column vertical to its three horizontals, and no grid in the paper is boxed or fully gridded [table.rule_style].

One grid merges cells and it is the appendix sector grid, where each sector name occupies a cell spanning its four year rows and five group separators open the blocks; no grid bands its rows and none carries a diagonal header [table.merged_cells].

No grid puts a unit in its header: the body grids print a 'Units：' line above the table, the appendix grids a 'Unit:' line above the header, and Tables 5-1 and 5-2 declare no unit anywhere [table.units_in_header].
Not one grid aligns on the decimal point - every numeric cell in the paper is centred, and the decimal points in Table 4-1's four columns land at eight different x positions [table.decimal_aligned].

Five grids leave the 424 pt measure, from 100.5 up to 109.5 per cent, and they leave it on opposite sides: Table 4-1 overhangs the LEFT margin by 21.6 pt while the appendix origins grid clears the right margin by 7 pt [table.width].
Every table is portrait and not one continues across a page break, including the twenty-one-row appendix grid that fills three quarters of its page [table.orientation].

No artwork in this paper is three-dimensional and none is a scatter, box, histogram, heatmap, network or photograph: the fourteen figure rows are five bar charts, six line charts, two choropleths and one flowchart [geometry.family].

Both maps are choropleths with a continuous colour ramp and they are the paper's only two colourbars - the Grid Modernization Index map and the final-scores map, each with four ticks [geometry.colorbar].

Legends split five inside, five outside to the right and four absent, and three of the four absences are the same defect at a different scale: the two fitness panels and the two-panel prediction figure distinguish their series by colour and dash only [geometry.legend].

One printed figure spans two measured boxes - Figure 5-2's 2025 and 2050 fitness curves - and the two rows are linked by `is_panel_of`; Figure 4-11 is the mirror case, two panels inside a single box [geometry.panel_count].

Only two rows print a number on the artwork, both the FMAX callout on a fitness panel; every other readable number in the paper is an axis tick or a grid cell, and Figure 4-10's ranking cannot be read off the map at all [geometry.data_labels].

Boxes truncate systematically rather than randomly: the plot detections on pages 7, 8, 9 and 11 stop short of axis labels, tick labels and captions, while the boxes on pages 5, 8, 10, 12 and 13 coincide exactly with PDF image-XObject rects [place.area_frac].

Placement is by section role: profiles and maps sit under 4.2.x, all four ranking and prediction tables under 4.3.2 and 4.4, the compact grids under 5.1.2, the flowchart and fitness curves under 5.1.1, and the appendix holds nothing but grids [place.section_path].
Exhibits cluster by section kind - result 19, model 1, test 3, symbols 1, appendix 2 - and the one symbols-kind exhibit is the nomenclature grid that also owns its caption [place.section_kind].

Eight of the twenty-six rows are introduced by printed number and eighteen by deixis ('as below', 'as follows', 'shown in figure 4-4'), so this team cites by number about a third of the time [mention.style].

Two numbered references point BACKWARD at artwork already printed - 'As can be seen from the figure 4-2' on the page that draws it and 'Figure 4-3 reveals' one page after it - which is why one row carries a zero lead and one a negative one [mention.lead_pages].
One citation crosses a page: Table 3-1 is cited on page 5 and printed on page 6, the only exhibit in the paper introduced before the page that draws it [mention.first_page].

Lead sentences are short and deictic - 'The prediction charts are as follows:', 'The algorithm flow is as follows:' - and they outnumber readings two to one: thirteen rows quote the sentence that introduces the artwork and only seven quote a reading after it, because this team mostly stops at the caption [mention.trail_sentence].

Two printed tables have no measured region and one measured box holds two grids, so table rows and printed tables diverge by three: Table 3-2 on page 6, the appendix TEC grid on page 24, and the unit-price grid fused into the same box as the sector grid [place.page_order].
